purpose: Offer optional task-sensitive subagent preferences while deciding model capability and reasoning effort independently. Preserve user root and personal configuration, then validate actual host availability before dispatch.

personal_config_policy.sync_advice: Review personal starting preferences manually after installing a changed Playbook policy. Project seed and upgrades never rewrite them.

host_effort_contract.validation: Use only values reported for the selected model by the current host. A UI label is normalized before dispatch and is not an additional host effort value.

supervisor_executor_local_override.conflict_action: Pause affected dispatch and ask once whether the user's route applies only to this task or to future Playbook tasks. A legacy generic preference is only a candidate, never an already confirmed persistent role route.
supervisor_executor_local_override.pending_result_policy: A needs_confirmation result exposes the candidate and confirmation binding, but no dispatchable route. Only a same-role, same-task_ref status=ready resolution issued by resolve_role contains route and a process-local dispatch capability; callers must not construct a ready result from a pending candidate or repository default.
supervisor_executor_local_override.confirmation_binding: A this_task or future choice must record scope, role, task_ref, SHA-256 digest of the exact candidate route and a locatable user-choice evidence_ref. This-task confirmation expires when the task, role or candidate changes; a task choice equal to the repository default still needs confirmation if it bypasses a conflicting local route. Future confirmation writes only the exact chosen route into the user-managed file.
supervisor_executor_local_override.persistent_write_scope: Only the user-managed local file may be changed after a future-scope choice; never edit this distributed repository config for a personal choice.

supervisor_executor_task_adequacy.selection_input: select_step verifies the resolver-issued process-local HMAC capability binding confirmation scope, role, task_ref, source and route digest, then checks current-task and exact-step adequacy. Pending, caller-crafted ready dictionaries, cross-task ready, mutated ready routes, or raw route dictionaries fail closed. Re-run resolve_role after a process restart or resumed task using the current local config and applicable user confirmation; the capability only guards in-process handoff and does not prove user consent or host dispatch.
supervisor_executor_task_adequacy.selection_rule: Use a fresh assessment tied to the current task_ref and each exact model/effort. Skip a proven insufficient available step; an unknown earlier available step blocks dispatch. Select only an available step with adequate evidence for the current task.
supervisor_executor_task_adequacy.escalation_rule: Escalation needs model_insufficient diagnosis and an insufficient assessment for the exact current model/effort; an unbound free-text adequacy statement is not evidence for another step.
supervisor_executor_task_adequacy.supervisor_fallback_gate: Use 5.6 Sol only when no 6 Sol model/effort is both host-available and assessed adequate; unknown available 6 Sol adequacy blocks fallback.
supervisor_executor_task_adequacy.executor_fallback_gate: Use 5.6 Terra only when every 6 Luna primary model/effort is host-unavailable. Proven Luna insufficiency alone does not open Terra; the Luna Max to 6 Sol path still requires an actual Max insufficiency diagnosis.

supervisor_executor_v2_scope.other_role_policy: The v2 generic profiles, task classes, transition policy and Reviewer route remain unchanged.
supervisor_executor_v2_scope.generic_substitution_exception: The user-approved Supervisor/Executor route is a scoped exception to the generic no-fixed-ladder, Luna opt-in and Sol-optional preferences; it does not change those preferences for other roles.
supervisor_executor_v2_scope.ordered_route_is_preference: The user-approved role route is an ordered preference, not automatic escalation. Every effort/model increase needs diagnosed model insufficiency and an evidence reference.
supervisor_executor_v2_scope.diagnosis: Fix environment, permission, goal and method problems at their source before considering a model or effort increase.
supervisor_executor_v2_scope.initial_executor_high_exception: The user-approved Executor starting effort is high for this role; this scoped exception supersedes the generic elevated_effort_policy starting point.
supervisor_executor_v2_scope.cross_model_initial_effort_exception: The user-approved Executor Luna-to-Sol route begins at Sol high only after evidenced Luna max insufficiency; this scoped exception supersedes the generic cross_model_upgrade initial low effort. When no 6 Luna combination is available, use the listed 5.6 Terra fallback only with fresh exact-step adequacy evidence.
supervisor_executor_v2_scope.availability_and_readback: Require fresh host model/effort availability, task adequacy and actual dispatched model/effort readback before side effects.

post_upgrade_effort_increase.reason: The stronger model at its initial effort did not satisfy a named acceptance or reduce the diagnosed uncertainty.

elevated_effort_policy: High and above require a concrete unresolved risk, failure, or post-upgrade acceptance-gap evidence reference. A broad complexity label alone is insufficient.
future_model_replacement: Update optional profile preferences after host availability and task-adequacy evidence. preferred_efforts are preferences, not a claim about all supported host efforts.
availability_evidence: Read the actual host model and supported effort before dispatch; defaults are suggestions, never an allowlist.
cost_preference: Use the lowest total cost expected to meet acceptance, including setup, non-cached input, rework and missed risk. This preference never blocks a capable configured root from performing a check.
substitution_policy: No automatic downgrade or fixed model ladder. An unavailable preferred model requires fresh host model/effort readback and task-adequacy evidence for the replacement; otherwise pause only dependent dispatch. FAST/Luna is opt-in evaluation, and Sol is an optional measured alternative rather than a mandatory step.
